what_it_does: Finding similar vectors in massive databases (vector similarity search—critical for AI retrieval, recommendation, and semantic search) normally requires comparing a query vector against millions of candidates, which is expensive in both memory and energy. This paper tackles the problem using NAND flash memory modified to perform comparisons on-chip. The innovation is a hybrid matching approach: first, an exact-search mode acts as a fast filter, comparing the query against all candidate vectors and eliminating clearly dissimilar ones using small multi-bit cells. Only the survivors then undergo expensive approximate-search mode comparisons with higher precision. The system also optimizes the threshold voltages and encoding schemes to reduce power while maintaining accuracy.
